Consider the following PR description:
Please support header rows in RestructuredText output
### Description

It would be great if the following would work:

```Python
>>> from astropy.table import QTable
>>> import astropy.units as u
>>> import sys
>>> tbl = QTable({'wave': [350,950]*u.nm, 'response': [0.7, 1.2]*u.count})
>>> tbl.write(sys.stdout,  format="ascii.rst")
===== ========
 wave response
===== ========
350.0      0.7
950.0      1.2
===== ========
>>> tbl.write(sys.stdout,  format="ascii.fixed_width", header_rows=["name", "unit"])
|  wave | response |
|    nm |       ct |
| 350.0 |      0.7 |
| 950.0 |      1.2 |
>>> tbl.write(sys.stdout,  format="ascii.rst", header_rows=["name", "unit"])

1. `self.write_header(lines, table.meta)` - calls `self.header.write(lines)` which for FixedWidthHeader is a no-op (pass)

Looking at the `FixedWidthData.write` method output (from fixedwidth.py line 261):
- First come the header rows (e.g., "name" row, then "unit" row)
- Then comes the position line (the `===` line)
- Then come data lines

So for a single header_row=["name"], `super().write()` returns:
```

lines[1]: "===== ========"         # position line
lines[2]: "350.0      0.7"         # data
lines[3]: "950.0      1.2"         # data
```

Then RST.write does `[lines[1]] + lines + [lines[1]]`:
```
"===== ========"                    # position line (prepended)
" wave response"                    # name header
"===== ========"                    # position line
"350.0      0.7"                    # data
"950.0      1.2"                    # data
"===== ========"                    # position line (appended)
```

For multiple header_rows=["name", "unit"], the output from `super().write()` would be:
```

lines[1]: "   nm       ct"         # unit header
lines[2]: "===== ========"         # position line

lines[4]: "950.0      1.2"         # data
